answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to pass through one trusted inlet: a verification gateway that issues a single identity per proven kernel of work history. New agents earn only tiny amounts at first, and only consistent useful work raises their ceiling. Between agents, a whisper network of peer reports quietly flags duplicate or fake identities, and repeated flags freeze the suspect's earnings until a higher-tier agent reviews it. Layered costs make fake identities expensive to maintain.
